title: Traffic Skein: braided replication prober for safe replicated inference
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a new replicated-traffic prober (Traffic Skein) that safely duplicates production requests into an isolated ingestion plane for model experiments (canaries, A/B, offline evals) with tenant-safe budgeting, stratified sampling, and automated divergence-triggered rollback hooks.
background: We need a robust way to exercise candidate models in near-production conditions without blowing cost or risking tenant interference. Current approaches (ad-hoc mirroring, full replication for short bursts) either lack stratification, provide poor tenant isolation, or require manual bookkeeping. Traffic Skein will provide a first-class primitive for: probabilistic, stratified duplication; per-tenant credit accounting and hard fences; a separate execution plane for replicated traffic; and automated signal-based rollback hooks for rollout tooling.
proposed_design: High level: insert a lightweight replication controller at the gateway layer that emits a braided stream: primary request continues to the live path; probes are copied to a dedicated "ingestion plane" through a secure, rate-limited side channel. The controller attaches a replication token and sampling vector to each copy to enable grouped analysis.

Sampling: use stratified reservoir sampling keyed by (tenant_id, route, hash(prefix)) to preserve representativeness across high-cardinality tenants while keeping overall replicate volume bounded. Tunable reservoir sizes per-tenant via credit buckets.

Budgeting & tenant isolation: per-tenant token bucket stored in Redis with strong enforcement at the controller. Each duplicated request consumes credits based on a configurable cost weight (short request vs long streaming). When budget is exhausted the controller either (a) drop replicated copies for that tenant, or (b) throttle to 0.1% fallback depending on tier. All billing tags are attached to replication copies so accounting pipelines can attribute costs immediately.

Execution plane: replicated requests go to a separate cluster pool (ingestion plane) that is logically and physically isolated from production serving. Ingestion plane will run relaxed SLOs, ephemeral resources, and no billing-side effects to upstream clients. KV cache sharing is disabled; we replay from cold-state unless explicit cache-warm modes are enabled for specific experiments.

Safety & privacy: before duplication the controller runs a PII redaction step and strips any write-intent flags. We will enforce a data-loss prevention (DLP) policy that drops examples failing redaction. Logs from ingestion plane are tagged and routed to secure storage with shorter retention.

Observability & divergence detection: every replicated request emits paired metrics (latency, token usage, top-level response hash, structured tags). A divergence detector computes rolling cohort-level deltas (distributional shifts, output drift, failure rate delta). If divergence exceeds a config threshold for a sustained window, the controller emits a webhook to the rollout manager to trigger auto-rollback or pause.

API: a simple control API will expose create/modify/delete for replication rules (route selectors, tenant overrides, sampling profile, cost weight, retention policy). Control plane changes are eventually consistent with enforcement local to gateway nodes.

Operational modes: "audit-only" (no cost accounted), "metered" (charges attributed to internal test budget), and "billable" (tagged costs materialize to tenant billing; used only with explicit tenant opt-in).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (MVP, 2 sprints): implement controller at gateway with pass-through duplication to a local replication queue; basic reservoir sampler keyed by tenant_id; per-tenant token bucket enforcement; ingestion plane consumer that writes to a sandbox cluster.
Phase 2 (1 sprint): add PII redaction pipeline, replication tagging, billing tag propagation, and basic dashboard for replication traffic volumes.
Phase 3 (1-2 sprints): divergence detector, webhook integration with rollout manager, config API, and canary rule templates.
Phase 4 (post-MVP): support for streaming responses, cache-warm modes, tenant opt-in billing, and GA hardening (load tests, chaos testing).
acceptance_criteria: Controller can duplicate production traffic at sustained 10k rps with mean added tail latency < 1ms at the gateway node under normal load.
Sampling preserves per-tenant distribution: synthetic test with 500 tenants shows sampled ratios per-tenant within 5% of expected for reservoir sizes >= 1000.
Token-bucket enforcement prevents replicated consumption above configured tenant budgets; tests show hard-drop semantics during budget exhaustion.
Ingestion plane is logically isolated: no requests or failures propagate back to primary path in all fault-injection scenarios.
Divergence detector triggers rollback webhook in synthetic divergence test and rollout manager performs pause/rollback within configured SLA ( < 2 minutes ).
PII redaction passes test corpus and examples failing redaction are recorded and dropped; infra team validates DLP logs and retention settings.
risks: Added CPU/latency at gateway under peak load could increase production costs; mitigated by sampling, reservoir caps, and adaptive backpressure.
Incorrect sampling configuration could bias tests; require conservative defaults and telemetry to detect skew.
Billing/chargeback mistakes could accidentally bill customers for replicated traffic; default to audit-only for GA and require tenant opt-in for billable mode.
PII escape risks; mitigated by DLP and failing-closed replication when redaction cannot be verified.
Tight coupling with rollout manager for auto-rollback could cause flapping; include hysteresis and safe windows to avoid oscillation.
test_plan: Unit tests for sampler, token-bucket, and redaction logic.
Integration tests: end-to-end replication through gateway -> replication queue -> ingestion plane using test harness that replays synthetic traffic with tenant combos.
Load tests: scale to 10k rps replicated volume at staging with realistic shard count; measure latency p95 and error propagation.
Chaos tests: network partitions between gateway and ingestion plane, and failure modes for consumer; assert main path unaffected.
Divergence simulation: inject controlled output drift and verify webhook + rollback behavior with rollout manager in a staging canary.
rollouts: Start in 'audit-only' mode for 2 weeks on a small subset (5 internal tenants) to validate sampling and tagging.
Expand to internal beta tenants with metered mode and monitor cost dashboards for 1 week.
Enable canary integration: link a canary rollout to the Traffic Skein rule with divergence thresholds; run for 24h and verify automated rollback behavior under synthetic divergence.
Gradual ramp to GA with tenant opt-in for billable mode only after billing checks and security review.
observability: Replication metrics: per-route replicated_rps, replicate_success, replicate_drop_reasons, per-tenant_credit_consumed.
Divergence metrics: response_hash_mismatch_rate, output_entropy_delta, error_rate_delta (replica vs primary), alerting on sustained deltas.
Tracing: paired trace IDs for primary+replica flows to enable end-to-end latency attribution; traces for redaction failures.
Dashboards: replication volume, per-tenant usage, cost forecast, and PII-redaction failure rate.
Audit logs: control API changes, replication rule CRUD, and billing-tag propagation events.
infra_changes: Lightweight replication queue (Kafka topic or Redis stream) per-region for buffered delivery to ingestion plane.
Dedicated ingestion cluster pool and autoscaling group with separate autoscale policies to avoid contention with primary serving.
Redis-backed per-tenant token buckets with strong consistency mode for enforcement.
Short retention secure storage for ingestion logs with access audit enabled.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Aisha Raman: Initial RFC posted. Key constraints: per-tenant hard fences, separate execution plane, and automated rollback hooks. Requested feedback on sampler design.

2025-02-18 - Design review (PM + Infra): PM suggests default to audit-only and add explicit tenant opt-in for billable mode. Infra requested a clear cost model for ingestion plane and suggested reservoir sampling rather than naïve probability sampling.
2025-02-22 - Miguel Ortega: Prototype of sampler merged to feature branch. Early microbench shows <0.5ms added median at gateway for single-copy flow; need to validate under higher concurrency.
2025-02-26 - Security review notes: require DLP gating + retention policy; suggested redaction library and unit tests for edge cases. Security review requested before canary expansion.
2025-03-01 - QA: Integration test harness ready; found an edge-case where streaming responses lost termination marker in replication path. Investigating fix in consumer logic.
